title: The Building Is a Clock
text: One Big Clock is an independent homage to Time, the 2027 show planned for this building. Here the whole building keeps one day, from ten in the morning, when the doors open, to seven, when they close. One frame every five minutes, one hour a minute. Watch the rod's shadow jump, and listen for the hour. Tap the rod to skip ahead.

title: Timetable
text: An ordinary day is a timetable. Reading a caption, crossing a street, making a rice ball. The board turns its page every few seconds, and every leaf falls into place one frame at a time. Tap the board to turn it yourself.

title: Twelve Frames
text: Stop-motion is time cut into stills. Twelve frames on the stair wall make one bounce, lit one at a time. At two frames a second you see the cuts. At twenty-four you see a ball. Tap a frame to change the speed.

title: A Day, a Week, a Year
text: Three hands on the gallery floor. First they keep the building's own hour. Then a week passes in fourteen seconds, then a whole year in twenty-four, and the day hand turns too fast to follow. Then one low bell, and nothing. Tap the centre to change the speed.

title: Ten Times Longer
text: Every step along this line is ten times longer than the last. A second, a caption, a rice ball, a visit, a day, a rice season, this building, and roughly three thousand years of rice in Japan. Listen as the ticks slow and fall. Tap a dot to read it.

title: Waiting for the Light
text: Some time we only spend waiting. The light counts down, the room goes quiet, the last seconds tick louder. Then everything moves at once. Tap the post to press the button.

title: One Stone
text: The last room is almost silent. One ordinary stone, and a light that circles it, one frame a second. Stay for one full turn. Nothing else happens, and that is the point.
